after.meaning: This leader commitment object has advanced its monotonically increasing quorum match index to an index at least startIndex, using only its current voter map.

identity.owner: commitment object allocated on leader entry

after.validity_context: In-memory leader-term commitment object; current voter set may be replaced while surviving voter match values are retained. Not a statement that FSM application completed.
after.durability: The accounting object is volatile; its supporting entries are reported after storage or successful replication.
after.recovery: Fresh leader entry rebuilds accounting from zero and requires current-term replication; old object is not reused.

formation.explanation: Leader dispatch assigns term/index, persists logs and records local match. Replication success records peer match in the term-specific commitment object. The configured voter order statistic advances commitment only after reaching the current-term startIndex. Main-loop notification enqueues committed inflight entries to the FSM and propagates commit index in later AppendEntries. Followers validate predecessor history, replace conflicts and apply through the bounded leader commit index. Future completion and application occur asynchronously after enqueue.

context.explanation: Follower timeout can start a voter election. Pre-vote normally precedes persisted term advancement and actual votes. Each election has its own reply channel; requestVote checks candidate membership, term, durable vote and log freshness. Quorum grants acquire leader role. Incoming higher-term requests and replication replies can cause loss of authority. Leader entry creates fresh accounting; exit stops replicators and fails outstanding operations. Leadership transfer and concurrent heartbeat dispatch require further tracing.

connection.explanation: Only voters in the current configuration contribute to formation. Reconfiguration is serialized behind committed membership and a current-term entry, then changes quorum eligibility while retaining surviving IDs support. Old replication completions target their captured old commitment object rather than a new leader object. Persistent logs and snapshot metadata constrain future freshness and reconstruction; losing a future does not erase a potentially surviving log entry. Snapshot restoration resets application/history context only after FSM restore completion.
